title: Query language
statement: Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean alphabet, let $c_0$ be a natural number, and let $b$ be a Boolean. For each Boolean string $x$, let $r(x)$ be the reduction output. If $b$ is true, the language contains exactly the indexed pairs $(x,i)$ with $i<|r(x)|$; if $b$ is false, it contains exactly the pairs $(x,i)$ for which the $i$th entry of $r(x)$ is true, taking an out-of-range entry to be false.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean alphabet
caveat: The snippet does not define the indexed-language construction.
